We demonstrate that REMC-driven magnetic stochasticity can reduce the RE current by over an order-of-magnitude when compared to unmitigated disruptions. The final termination is mediated via a post-thermal-quench "cold" vertical displacement of the plasma, which, together with magnetic stochasticity, increases RE losses via scrape-off once the plasma contacts the first wall. These results demonstrate a viable mechanism for RE mitigation using passively driven plasma instabilities on high-current tokamaks.

papers.title: Marginalization-Based Regularization for Separable Nonlinear Least Squares Problems with Applications to Semi-Blind Deblurring
papers.authors: Jordan T. Dworaczyk; Malena I. Español
papers.abstract: Separable nonlinear least squares problems arise in inverse problems such as semi-blind image deblurring, where the image enters the forward model linearly, and the blur parameters enter nonlinearly. Even when the image is regularized, joint estimation of the image and blur parameters can favor a degenerate no-blur solution, in which the blur operator tends to the identity and the reconstruction merely denoises the data without removing the blur. We address this by regularizing the blur parameters. Motivated by the determinant term arising from Gaussian marginalization, we construct a family of blur-parameter priors whose weight and auxiliary operators can be chosen independently of the image prior. The resulting log-determinant penalty is incorporated into regularized variable projection, which eliminates the image variables by minimization. Under periodic boundary conditions and assuming the matrices involved admit a joint spectral decomposition, we show that a sufficiently large determinant weight rules out the no-blur solution as a local minimizer. We also characterize the regularizer's behavior as the auxiliary regularization scale tends to zero or infinity. We solve the reduced problem with a quasi-Newton method that evaluates the objective and its derivatives in the Fourier domain. In experiments with Gaussian, defocus, and motion blur, the proposed prior improves image and blur recovery over Gaussian marginalization across several settings, with determinant weights computed from the true image. A single-sample experiment illustrates how to automatically choose parameters from the data using a conditional generalized cross-validation criterion.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Large-Scale Velocity Field from DESI DR1 with Bayesian Inference
papers.authors: Raeed Mundow; Adi Nusser
papers.abstract: Survey boundaries and nonlinear dynamics complicate reconstruction of large-scale matter-density and peculiar-velocity fields from galaxy redshift surveys. We develop and compare two reconstruction methods within a common Bayesian framework, based on linear perturbation theory and the Zel'dovich approximation, and apply them to the DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey. We infer the initial density field using a Gaussian prior and likelihood, with the Zel'dovich model displacing particles from a uniform Lagrangian grid. Both yield maximum a posteriori (MAP) fields; only the linear posterior is sampled. Our main findings are: \textit{(i)} Both reconstructions yield similar large-scale density structures and coherent velocity patterns in the survey interior, beyond roughly \(50\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\) from the footprint boundaries. \textit{(ii)} Comparison with Cosmicflows-4 groups, predominantly from the SDSS Fundamental Plane sample in the DESI overlap, shows close agreement between mean observed radial velocities and MAP predictions when binned by the latter, despite substantial individual scatter. \textit{(iii)} Both yield similar reflex-dipole profiles, defined as mean shell velocities relative to those at randomly sampled centres, out to \(\sim225\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\). The profiles depend weakly on the prior normalization \(σ_8\), but lie below the fiducial linear \(Λ\)CDM reference at \(r<50\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\). Sparse sampling limits the largest radii. \textit{(iv)} In an exploratory BAO test, shifting galaxies and randoms to a target redshift \(z=8\) using reconstructed displacements sharpens the acoustic feature in both cases, with a slightly more pronounced peak for Zel'dovich. Survey geometry and galaxy bias remain the principal limitations.

papers.title: GSPIM: A Temporal-Locality-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting Accelerator with Polymorphic PIM and Multi-Frame Rendering Dataflow
papers.authors: Zirui Ma; Zhihua Fan; Haibin Wu; Dongrui Fan; Xiaochun Ye et al.
papers.abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) enables high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis for dynamic scenes, supporting free-viewpoint video, mobile XR, and autonomous systems at the edge. Methods using explicit 4D distributions, keyframe interpolation, or anchor binding share two GPU data-movement bottlenecks. Temporal filtering follows model record loading, wasting LPDDR5 bandwidth on inactive data. Frame-isolated execution also overlooks highly overlapping active sets and depth relationships across adjacent frames, reloading shared attributes when working sets exceed on-chip cache capacity. To address these bottlenecks, we present GSPIM, a temporal-locality-aware 4DGS accelerator for PIM-enabled edge devices. Polymorphic PIM adapts a shared near-memory datapath to representation-specific field layouts and selection procedures. It filters and compacts valid data into contiguous inputs before the GPU accesses complete attributes, reducing ineffective transfers. Multi-Frame Rendering Dataflow reuses active attributes and stable depth relationships within a temporal window, reducing repeated work across frames. Hybrid Dataflow Scheduling overlaps near-memory data preparation with GPU rendering to reduce waiting. Evaluation combines a GPU-PIM model calibrated to Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB with a 1z DRAM physical implementation of the added circuits. Across three 4DGS methods and six dynamic scenes, GSPIM achieves a 4.15x geometric-mean speedup and a 4.99x geometric-mean energy-efficiency improvement over a fully optimized frame-by-frame GPU baseline. The maximum scene-level PSNR difference is 0.011 dB, and the added physical footprint is 18.7172 square millimeters across 32 LPDDR5 dies.

papers.title: On the Onsager--Machlup functional of the infinite-dimensional angular central Gaussian distribution and related measures
papers.authors: Hefin Lambley; T. J. Sullivan; Sam Taylor
papers.abstract: The Onsager--Machlup functional of a probability measure is a generalisation of the negative logarithm of the probability density function, defined precisely using the ratios of masses of balls in the limit of vanishing radius. It plays an important role in several areas of applied mathematics because its minimisers can be understood as modes of the measure. We show that the Onsager--Machlup functional of the angular central Gaussian measure on the unit sphere of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space---i.e., the radial projection of a centred Gaussian measure with covariance operator $C$---is constant on the finite-dimensional sphere spanned by the eigenvectors of leading eigenvalue under $C$, and takes the value $+\infty$ elsewhere. We discuss the consequences of this extreme concentration of mass for maximum a posteriori estimation in Bayesian inverse problems with an angular central Gaussian prior.

papers.title: Crossover from Schwarzian dynamics to rotational soft modes in near-extremal Lovelock black holes
papers.authors: Ankit Anand; Aditya Singh; Kimet Jusufi
papers.abstract: Near-extremal black holes are controlled by a small set of soft modes, and counting these modes fixes the coefficient of $\log T$ in the entropy. We ask whether genuine six-derivative interactions change that count, working in seven-dimensional third-order Lovelock gravity, the simplest setting where the cubic Lovelock term is dynamical. The multiplicities stay the same, but the naive count fails. At fixed charge the Maxwell mode is frozen out, and the fifteen rotational modes of the $S^5$ act as a quantum rotor that only switches on above the scale $K_J^{-1}$. As a result, the coefficient of $\log T$ runs from $3/2$ at the lowest temperatures to $9$ above that scale, and never reaches the naive Gaussian value $19/2$. We compute the moment of inertia $K_J$ from the charged slow-rotation solution and find that the Lovelock couplings move the crossover without changing the multiplicities. Only large AdS black holes have a wide window in which the full rotational contribution competes with the classical entropy. Adding a probe charged scalar, we derive an analytic near-horizon Schwinger threshold in the cubic coupling. Its large-AdS limit tells us when the broad rotational crossover window can coexist with the absence of a charged-scalar Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound violation.

papers.title: VISAGE: Vertex-based Intrinsic Surface Appearance GEneration via Dual-Stream Diffusion for Arbitrary 3D Heads
papers.authors: Jeremias Krauß; Pragati Jaiswal; René Schuster; Didier Stricker
papers.abstract: Recovering identity-faithful, physically based surface appearance for 3D human heads from sparse images remains challenging. Existing methods often rely on UV-based pipelines, introducing seam artefacts, or operate in image space, limiting surface consistency. We present VISAGE, Vertex-based Intrinsic Surface Appearance GEneration, a surface-based conditional diffusion framework that synthesises per-vertex albedo and roughness directly on arbitrary mesh topologies, without requiring consistent UV parameterisation at training time. VISAGE combines global spectral processing with local geodesic K-Nearest-Neighbour refinement, enforcing structural coherence while restoring detail beyond the truncated spectral basis. Multi-view RGB images condition the network via visibility-aware cross-attention, enabling occlusion-robust synthesis across the full head surface. Region-specific modules specialise in semantically demanding and distinct areas (eyes, mouth, skin and hair), while a tangent-space output projection recovers fine iris detail. We further introduce a scalable procedural augmentation pipeline that enriches raw geometry scans with physically plausible albedo, roughness and normal maps for training. The predicted attributes render directly as a single RGBA vertex-colour channel. VISAGE reduces FID by 42.7% on NPHM and 22.5% and 4.4% on zero-shot FaceVerse and i3DMM, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline, with a 7.2M-parameter core network.

papers.title: Rate-Distortion-Perception Tradeoff for Vector Gaussian Sources with Limited Common Randomness: Exact Characterization and Approximate Universality
papers.authors: Wentao Wang; Shuo Shao; Ruibin Li; Jingjing Qian; Jun Chen et al.
papers.abstract: The distortion-rate-common randomness-perception (DRCP) theory characterizes how limited common randomness (CR) improves reconstruction fidelity under perceptual constraints, thereby providing an information-theoretic foundation for generative compression. In this paper, we characterize the DRCP tradeoff for vector Gaussian sources with limited CR under the squared-error distortion measure and the squared Wasserstein-2 perception measure. Specifically, we first establish a generalized reverse waterfilling characterization of globally optimal allocations. Second, we derive an analytical upper bound on the DRCP function through sequential greedy allocation of rate and CR. For fixed rate and CR budgets, the resulting representation is independent of the perception threshold. Finally, we establish its approximate universality through uniform performance guarantees: the achievable distortion exceeds the optimal distortion by at most $2ρ^*\approx0.2897$ times the total source variance, whereas the optimal-to-greedy distortion ratio is at least $η^*\approx0.7517$.

papers.title: Missing Outer Rings in the exoALMA Sample: Physical Mechanisms Suppressing Dust Ring Formation Despite Strong Pressure Bumps
papers.authors: Lilian Luo; Paola Pinilla; Jochen Stadler
papers.abstract: The exoALMA survey has revealed candidate gas pressure bumps at radii beyond the observed millimetre continuum discs in several protoplanetary systems, raising the question of whether these regions could host undetected dust structures. We investigate this for nine of the exoALMA discs by reconstructing gas surface density profiles from midplane pressure gradient measurements derived from $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO ALMA Band 7 observations. We evolve the dust using DustPy across a grid of turbulence and fragmentation parameters ($α\in \{10^{-4}, 10^{-3}\}$; $v_\mathrm{frag} \in \{1, 10\}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$), followed by radiative transfer calculations with RADMC-3D to give predictions for the continuum emission. We find that the dominant outcome across the explored parameter space is efficient outer dust trapping, leading to prominent outer continuum rings that should be detectable at ALMA Band 7, in tension with the observations. The $^{13}$CO-based reconstructions almost universally produce detectable outer rings, whereas the $^{12}$CO-based reconstructions show more variation. We further test delayed formation of the outer pressure bump and enhanced outer-disc turbulence as possible suppression mechanisms of ring formation. Enhanced turbulence weakens the predicted outer continuum emission most effectively, although the efficiency of the mechanism depends on the system explored and on where the turbulence transition is placed. Delayed bump formation generally does not prevent rapid outer dust accumulation.

papers.title: Phase-DGS: Phase-guided Dynamic Gaussian Splatting from Unsynchronized Multi-view Video
papers.authors: Hosung Jeon; Jun Young Jeong; Sangwoon Kwak; Joonsoo Kim; Sangmin Kim et al.
papers.abstract: Spatiotemporal scene reconstruction with Dynamic Gaussian Splatting (DGS) fundamentally depends on perfect temporal synchronization across all cameras, an assumption rarely achievable in practice. Industry-standard synchronization requires expensive specialized hardware and complex setup, while data-driven alternatives including audio-based alignment, geometry matching, and pose tracking remain limited by restrictive environmental or scene-specific assumptions. To overcome these limitations, we propose Phase-DGS, a framework that replaces conventional timestamps with a semantic phase representing each frame's inherent state within the underlying motion cycle. Frames capturing the same motion state share the same phase regardless of which camera records them or when, naturally establishing spatiotemporal correspondence across unsynchronized cameras. We validate Phase-DGS under temporal offsets, frame drops, and camera freezes, achieving up to +8.5 dB PSNR improvement over baselines while enabling seamless integration with existing DGS backbones including RealTime-4DGS and FreeTimeGS.

papers.title: Leakage-free evaluation of residual graph convolutional networks for network intrusion detection
papers.authors: Zahid Iqbal
papers.abstract: Graph neural networks are increasingly proposed for network intrusion detection, yet many reported results come from protocols in which test flows shape the graph used for training, duplicated flows sit on both sides of the split, or a single split is reported. This study measures what a residual graph convolutional network gains over simpler models once these sources of optimism are removed. CICIDS2017 and NF-UNSW-NB15-v2 were cleaned with label-aware removal of exact duplicates, removing 69% of NF-UNSW-NB15-v2 flows. Flows were linked in a nearest-neighbour graph built from training flows only, and validation and test flows were attached to their nearest training flows at prediction time. A two-layer residual network was compared with eight models under the same settings, including a nearest-neighbour vote over the same graph, gradient-boosted trees and a random forest, over three seeds that each draw a new split, with ablations, leave-one-family-out and feature-noise tests. On CICIDS2017 the residual network reached a binary F1 of 98.11% (SD 0.18) and on NF-UNSW-NB15-v2 90.57% (0.38), indistinguishable from a multilayer perceptron without the graph and from other graph networks. Tree ensembles were 1.48 to 1.57 F1 points higher on CICIDS2017 and led on the area under the precision-recall curve on both datasets; their CICIDS2017 multiclass macro-F1 reached 93.08% against 64.51%, a gap mainly from benign flows the residual network assigned to small attack classes. No ablation, including transductive graph construction, changed F1 beyond seed variation. Under Gaussian feature noise (SD 0.5), the residual network kept an F1 of 96.16%, while XGBoost fell to 0.67%. Under a leakage-controlled protocol, message passing over flow graphs adds no measurable accuracy over a perceptron, and tree ensembles remain stronger on both; the advantage of graph models lies in robustness to feature noise.

papers.title: BhopalMLS: A LiDAR Dataset for Semantic Scene Understanding in Heterogeneous Urban Environments
papers.authors: Pyare Lal Chauhan; Vaibhav Kumar; Bharat Lohani
papers.abstract: We introduce BhopalMLS, a large-scale Mobile Laser Scanning (MLS) dataset from a dense, heterogeneous urban environment in Bhopal, India, with mixed traffic, informal structures, and narrow unplanned streets. It spans approximately 10 km of road corridors with over 1.2 billion points and 19,518 annotated instances across 62 fine-grained static categories, grouped into 12-class and 21-class benchmark taxonomies; 6 optional moving-class subclasses support dynamic-object analysis. Existing 3D datasets, collected in well-planned cities, are structurally more uniform than such unplanned settings, and lack their subtype diversity. On semantic and instance segmentation at both granularities, fine-tuned foundation models surpass supervised baselines: Utonia(L) reaches 71.28% mIoU (vs. PTv3's 68.04% from scratch) and 44.07% mAP50 on the 12-class benchmark. Cross-region experiments against four established datasets (Ke-MLS, Toronto-3D, Paris-Lille-3D, SemanticKITTI) reveal a consistent asymmetric transferability: models trained on BhopalMLS transfer better than the reverse on every pair, for both Utonia(L) and Concerto(L) (mean 21.5, up to 36 mIoU points), holding even when the target is denser. Factor-controlled retraining at a fixed label budget, repeated on both models, attributes this to the coverage of BhopalMLS's subtype inventory rather than to dataset size or corridor geometry: collapsing each class to a single subtype costs 13.0 and 13.3 mIoU points for Utonia(L) and Concerto(L). BhopalMLS therefore offers a testbed for 3D perception beyond well-planned cities. Data and an interactive viewer are at https://geoai4cities.github.io/bhopalmls.

papers.title: Non-asymptotic Sphere-Packing Bounds for Finite-Blocklength Scalar Gaussian Multiple-Access and Broadcast Channels
papers.authors: Kaixuan Bao; Wei Xu; Xiaohu You
papers.abstract: This paper investigates non-asymptotic achievable rate regions of Gaussian multiple-access channels (MACs) and broadcast channels (BCs) in the finite-blocklength regime. By employing a proposed volume-uniform random coding (VURC) codebook that distributes codewords uniformly within an $n$-dimensional power sphere, together with successive interference cancellation (SIC) decoding, we derive a closed-form achievability bound, a scheme-specific lower bound on the average error probability, and a fourth-order asymptotic characterization. The proposed SIC achievability bound admits a simple and analytically interpretable closed-form expression, enabling direct performance evaluation without iterative computation. The structure of the proposed SIC asymptotic bound offers a highly extensible framework, allowing advances in single-user finite-blocklength theory to be systematically incorporated into the multiuser setting. Futhermore, to characterize the performance benefit of joint decoding, we further derive numerical and closed-form achievability bounds for the two-user Gaussian MAC under joint nearest-neighbor (JNN) decoding. Numerical results illustrate the performance differences among the proposed SIC and JNN bounds and existing benchmarks.

papers.title: Sparse-View 3D Coronary Reconstruction from Vessel Segmentations Using a Diffusion Prior
papers.authors: Tianyuan Wang; Kenan Niu; Stefano Stramigioli
papers.abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) coronary anatomy from sparse angiographic views could support percutaneous coronary intervention, but limited angular coverage and imperfect vessel segmentations introduce substantial geometric ambiguity. We propose a vessel-specific reconstruction framework combining a learned 3D diffusion prior, visual-hull initialization, and projection-based data consistency. The unconditional diffusion model is trained on coronary vessel masks without paired 2D--3D data and reused across different view counts without retraining. During inference, a scaled visual hull initializes reconstruction, while projection-based updates constrain diffusion refinement using patient-specific vessel observations. We evaluated the framework on simulated angiograms derived from ImageCAS computed tomography angiography volumes using two, four, and eight views at two contrast levels. Across 50 evaluation coronary-tree cases, the proposed method achieved higher mean Dice and clDice than visual hull, deep image prior (DIP), and hash-grid implicit neural representation (INR) at all view counts under reduced contrast. With eight views, improvements over DIP, the best-performing baseline at lower contrast, were approximately 0.13 in Dice and 0.22 in clDice. At higher contrast, performance remained competitive with hash-grid INR, the best-performing eight-view baseline. The preferred diffusion starting timestep depended on observation quality and view count, with excessive refinement reducing accuracy at higher contrast. Projection guidance improved both metrics across all conditions. Averaging stochastic reconstructions further improved accuracy, while sample disagreement localized errors with average-precision gains of 0.14--0.21 over error prevalence. These findings support diffusion-prior reconstruction from sparse vessel observations, although clinical validation remains necessary.

papers.title: SCANO: Restoring Boundary-Condition Completeness in Sampled Meshes with a Sliced-Cross-Attention Neural Operator for 3D Thermal Fields
papers.authors: Tianyu Li; Zhiwei Cao; Qingang Zhang; Ruihang Wang; Binyang Song et al.
papers.abstract: Training neural operators on million-cell meshes can exceed GPU memory limits. Models are therefore trained on subsamples and deployed on whole meshes or selected regions. However, subsampling can distort boundary information, degrading accuracy. We ask when boundary conditioning under sampling stays consistent with whole-mesh training, and how to aggregate and inject boundary data. Representing the solution as an integral of boundary data against type-dependent measures, we show that subsampling distorts this conditioning in three ways: incomplete boundary coverage or a sample-dependent global state, face weighting by count rather than area, and compression of boundary inputs into a low-dimensional vector. This analysis yields four measurable consistency conditions checkable before training. We satisfy them with two backbone-agnostic modules. Boundary Quadrature Attention (BQA) aggregates all boundary faces, typed and area-weighted, into slice tokens that every query point reads at every layer. Anchored Global State (AGS) estimates the global state from anchors independent of the sampled points. Adding both to a scalable message-passing and slice-attention backbone yields SCANO. We evaluate the approach on controlled and public benchmarks and a data-centre thermal simulation dataset (DCTS) containing million-cell meshes. On both benchmarks, BQA improves every backbone, reducing whole-mesh error up to 15-fold. On all three datasets, AGS aligns regional with whole-mesh predictions, cutting regional error at least tenfold for most backbones on the public benchmark. Together, the modules nearly halve the best original backbone's whole-mesh error on both benchmarks. SCANO predicts a room-scale field in under one second, over 100 times faster than whole-room anchor self-attention.

papers.title: Multi-Path Mamba Diffusion for 3D Point Cloud Semantic Scene Completion
papers.authors: Li Liang; Naveed Akhtar; Jordan Vice; Anwaar Ulhaq; Ajmal Saeed Mian
papers.abstract: 3D semantic scene completion plays a critical role in enabling various downstream tasks within autonomous systems by estimating both missing geometric structures and semantic information in scene data. In this work, we introduce a unique neural framework that integrates state space modeling with diffusion-based generative approaches to enhance 3D point cloud semantic scene completion. We propose \textit{MPath Mamba} diffusion network, leveraging a skip-triple Mamba structure, dimensional decomposition residuals, and multi-directional dilations within multi-path data to efficiently process long-sequence data for feature extraction. The proposed method operates in the conditioned latent space of a variational autoencoder, enhanced by a state-space mechanism to improve 3D point cloud representation and reconstruction. Extensive experiments conducted on the SemanticKITTI benchmark demonstrate that our approach achieves highly competitive performance for 3D point cloud semantic scene completion.

papers.title: A general sharp-interface simulation framework for microstructure evolution
papers.authors: Albert Linda; Dierk Raabe
papers.abstract: Simulating microstructure evolution requires tracking many moving grain and phase boundaries coupled to thermodynamic and mechanical fields. We present Gaussian-projected kinetics (GPK), a sharp-interface framework in which every cell stores an integer grain or phase label. Near a boundary, a temporary Gaussian projection of the label map provides the interface normal and curvature and is then discarded. Capillarity, chemistry, stored energy, transport and elasticity move the boundaries through one topology-preserving update. Because the Gaussian measurement length is fixed in physical units, mesh refinement keeps a consistent capillary scale without a diffuse interface. GPK models grain growth, recrystallisation, multiphase evolution and elastic-coupled solidification in two and three dimensions. It is verified on analytical benchmarks and compared grain by grain with phase-field simulations, running 8.5 to 96 times faster at matched accuracy in our tests. An Al-Cu application with CALPHAD thermodynamic data connects it to measured recrystallisation and precipitation data.

papers.title: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models
papers.authors: Andrea Cenzato; Lukas Karch; Andre Luckow; Yoran Pichon; Francesco Pasqua et al.
papers.abstract: This paper presents a CFD dataset of a highly parametrized 3D wing operating in ground effect, designed for benchmarking neural surrogate models for aerodynamic prediction, using a wing shape and flow conditions typically encountered in motorsport applications. The dataset comprises 770 RANS simulations of 194 unique wing configurations, sampled across 27 airfoil profile variants and 4 distances from the ground, spanning variations in wing sweep, chord, taper, angle of attack, and tip twist. Six neural network architectures representing distinct paradigms --- convolutional (DoMINO), graph-based (X-MeshGraphNet), transformer-based (AB-UPT, GeoTransolver, GAOT), and JEPA-based (AeroJEPA) --- are evaluated on their ability to predict surface pressure coefficient and wall shear stress distributions, from which integral drag and lift coefficients are recovered. The dataset is intended to be used as a challenging benchmark for surrogate CFD models, due to the uniqueness of the ground effect being absent from other wing and airfoil datasets.

papers.title: Predicting Void Points in Self-Occluding Forest Volumes
papers.authors: Benjamin Bachmayr; Mohamed Youssef; Oliver Bimber
papers.abstract: Synthetic Aperture Imaging (SAI) enables drones to observe forest canopies by warping and averaging multiple displaced views at a common depth. However, occlusion is suppressed rather than eliminated, causing poorly observed regions to appear occupied and leading to systematic biomass overestimation. The Deep Forest project cannot distinguish reconstruction artifacts from real vegetation because its training data relies on measured reflectance points, excluding empty space and preventing the network from learning explicit occupancy boundaries.   This thesis addresses the problem by modifying training labels rather than the imaging process. Each simulated scene is rendered twice: as a 9x9 grid of top-down captures for focal-stack generation and as 550 depth-clipped slabs derived from scene geometry to provide occupancy labels, explicitly representing void space as a negative class. A Gazebo pipeline generates procedural forest stands containing 80-200 trees across three species. A pretrained Pix2Pix model translates rendered RGB images into a synthetic near-infrared band, and Light Field Rendering produces aligned focal stacks of 550 planes across three channels.   Four architectures were evaluated on a held-out scene. The plain 2D U-Net achieved an IoU of 0.6290, outperforming the volumetric 3D U-Net (0.5707). Established reconstruction methods performed substantially worse: COLMAP achieved 0.3446 and DepthAnything3 0.2959, both after their respective optimal dilation sweeps. An RGB-input variant of the volumetric architecture achieved the highest IoU of 0.6514 without dilation or per-scene calibration. These results highlight the limitations of conventional reconstruction methods, which recover visible surfaces but struggle to infer occupancy within closed canopies.

papers.title: CANDO: Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization for Residual Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Zeyu Gao; Chengkai Hou; Chaoyue Li; Zhuangzhe Wu; Jiaming Liu et al.
papers.abstract: Pretrained generative policies provide strong behavior priors for robot control, but adapting them efficiently with online reinforcement learning remains difficult. A central challenge is how to improve a frozen generative policy without destroying the structure learned from offline demonstrations. Noise-space residual methods address this by modifying the policy's input noise, but existing noise-space methods typically regulate adaptation through fixed latent feasible regions, which may exclude valuable noise edits. In contrast, action-space residual methods are more sample-efficient, but their efficiency can still be further improved. We propose Conservative Noise Directional Optimization (CNDO), a noise-space residual RL method that improves a frozen generative policy by learning state- and noise-conditioned directions around Gaussian latent samples. CNDO removes predefined latent feasible regions and instead regulates noise-space adaptation through the soft conservative constraint, which consists of conservative value estimation and gated execution. We further introduce Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization (CANDO), which adds an action-space residual, combining structured latent-space improvement with local action correction. Experiments show that, once CNDO narrows the gap between noise-space and action-space residual learning, CANDO further improves over single-space optimization, achieving 76.1 NAUC and a 91.4% final success rate, surpassing the best single-space results by 6.6 NAUC and 4.1% success rate. More demos and info are available on https://cando-rl.github.io/.

papers.title: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy
papers.authors: Kunal Kumar; Tomonori Shirakawa; Boseong Kim; Ryo Wakizaka; Ikko Hamamura et al.
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) accuracy remains limited for strongly correlated systems like iron-sulfur clusters. This accuracy heavily depends on the mean-field reference state, which determines the sampling ansatz and configuration-recovery target. We extend the qcsc-prefect workflow to support a broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock (BS-UHF) starting point, derived from atom-localized antiferromagnetic initial guesses. For the $[Fe_4S_4(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$ cubane (54 electrons, 36 orbitals, 72 data qubits; 88 total qubits), this lowers the mean-field reference by $\approx 534$ mHa relative to the Restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF) solution (-327.0809 vs. -326.5474 Ha). Combined with deep multi-step configuration recovery on ROQUO GPU nodes at subspace dimension $d = 3 \times 10^{10}$, we reach $E = -327.235076$ Ha. This is 4.3 mHa above the finite-$D = 4000$ DMRG value (-327.2393952 Ha) and $\sim 512-517$ mHa below a previous same-active-space RHF-reference SQD calculation. Extrapolating to the $d \to \infty$ limit via a Gaussian-in-log $d$ fitting ansatz gives an asymptotic estimate $E_\infty = -327.244468$ Ha $\pm 1.05$ mHa, just 0.33 mHa above our discarded-weight-extrapolated DMRG estimate ($E_{D\to\infty} = -327.244797$ Ha $\pm 0.46$ mHa), well within their combined $1σ$ uncertainty. We characterize the determinant-subspace composition driving convergence, show matching validation on $[Fe_2S_2(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$, and report multi-HPC execution on Fugaku, Miyabi-G, and ROQUO. We conclude that reference-state preparation, rather than subspace size alone, is a key driver of SQD energy accuracy under strong electronic correlation.

papers.title: On the propagation of chaos for three-dimensional Coulomb Brownian particles
papers.authors: Lei Li; Jian-Guo Liu
papers.abstract: While the mean field limit of the Brownian particles with 3D Coulomb interaction has been resolved starting from the Liouville equation, the justification directly from the random trajectories is not fully resolved. In our previous work (J. Math. Phys., 60, 111501, 2019), it has been shown that the time marginals of any limit point of the empirical measure form a weak solution to the mean field nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation. However, the identification to the strong solution is not established due to the lack of regularity. In this short note, we first make use of the variational formulation of the quadratic function to establish the desired space-time $L^2$ bound mentioned already in J. Math. Phys., 60, 111501, 2019. This fills gap and shows that the time marginals must be the must be the strong solution. Moreover, making use of the virial type estimates and the force dissipation, we also establish the propagation of chaos in path space directly from the random trajectories of the particle systems.

papers.title: Physical Diffusion Policy via MPM-Guided 3D Gaussian Simulation
papers.authors: Can Wang; Qiyuan Qiao; Lei Liu; Ge Yuan; Xinhui Liu et al.
papers.abstract: Learning robust manipulation policies for diverse everyday objects remains challenging because objects with different materials exhibit distinct deformation and contact dynamics. While diffusion policies provide a powerful framework for modeling multimodal manipulation behaviors, they typically lack explicit physical reasoning and may produce averaged actions when facing heterogeneous objects. We present a physics-aware diffusion policy that augments visual imitation learning with object physical understanding. Our framework recovers material properties from visual demonstrations by coupling 3D Gaussian Splatting with differentiable Material Point Method simulation, where video guidance and particle-level constraints enable accurate physical parameter estimation. The estimated physics conditions are further integrated into a material-aware Mixture-of-Experts diffusion policy, allowing adaptive behavior generation across different physical regimes. For practical deployment, we introduce a physics memory bank that provides efficient physical retrieval without requiring online simulation optimization. Experiments on a wide range of simulated and real-world objects demonstrate improved manipulation success and generalization over existing diffusion-based approaches. These results show that incorporating physical knowledge is critical for scalable robot manipulation in diverse environments.

papers.title: Hybrid Particle-Voxel Dynamics for Multimodal 3D World Simulation
papers.authors: Jimmy Wang; Yifan Chou; Kaifeng Zhang; Yixuan Wang; Binghao Huang et al.
papers.abstract: Predicting how the world evolves in response to robot actions is central to policy learning, evaluation, and planning. However, many action-conditioned world models predict future observations in 2D image or video space without explicitly modeling the underlying 3D scene, making spatial consistency across viewpoints and over long-horizon interactions challenging. We introduce 3D World Simulator, an action-conditioned multimodal world modeling framework that jointly predicts appearance, geometry, and tactile observations from a unified 3D representation. Our approach combines a hybrid particle-voxel autoencoder that compresses point clouds into compact 3D voxel latents with an action-conditioned latent dynamics model that predicts their evolution. The shared 3D representation supports geometrically consistent rendering from arbitrary viewpoints and flexible integration of spatially aligned tactile signals. Our experiments demonstrate interactive, long-horizon, multimodal prediction at 50 Hz. We then show how our model enables scalable data generation for policy training and evaluation using tactile and multi-view visual observations, including wrist-mounted and novel camera views. Furthermore, we scale our method to large datasets containing diverse objects and demonstrate model-based planning with unseen objects and robot configurations. Together, these results highlight the potential of hybrid particle-voxel dynamics as a foundation for multimodal 3D world simulation.

papers.title: A Parametric Linear Conic Projection for Structured Sparse Attention
papers.authors: Michel Barlaud; Clement Genninasca; Maxime Zanella; Benoit Macq; Benoit Legat
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Cone Alignment Index (CAI), a scale-invariant sparsity measure associated with a Lorentz-cone geometry. We provide a probabilistic analysis of the distribution of the CAI score, including a general theorem and explicit corollaries for Gaussian and uniform distributions. As a consequence, we show that, in the high-sparsity regime, the probability that the samples lie within the convex cone tends to one. Building upon this formulation, we derive two complementary projections: the \emph{Parametric Linear Conic Projection} (PLCP), an efficient closed-form approximation, and the \emph{Parametric Euclidean Conic Projection} (PECP), the exact Euclidean projection onto the cone boundary.   Our analysis establishes several fundamental theoretical properties. We prove that PLCP and PECP are collinear, differ only by a positive radial scaling factor, and induce exactly the same sparsity threshold, thereby preserving an identical active support. Furthermore, we derive a support-identification theorem showing that, for any prescribed sparsity level $l<n$, the number of coefficients discarded at each iteration is theoretically controlled.   Building on this theoretical foundation, we develop a bilevel PLCP framework for structured matrix sparsification. The proposed method naturally generates hardware-friendly structured sparsity patterns, including row-wise, column-wise, and diagonal masks, making it particularly well suited for accelerating Transformer attention mechanisms.

papers.title: Nuisance structure and the detection boundary for population size: how profiling can change a rate, not only a constant
papers.authors: Yakir Berchenko
papers.abstract: A system contains an unknown number $N$ of units, each failing at an unknown common rate, each unit is removed once it fails. The failure-rate declines as units are removed, but after only a few failures the decline is too slight to distinguish from a constant rate, and the maximum-likelihood estimate of $N$ is infinite with substantial probability. This is a well-known feature of the model, but its probability has not been quantified. We show that about $N^{2/3}$ failures are needed before a finite population can be distinguished from an inexhaustible one, and that at this scale the profile log-likelihood ratio converges to that of a Gaussian shift experiment, in which an infinite estimate occurs with a calculable probability. The exponent is not a property of the model alone. Profiling annihilates the Taylor terms that the nuisance-parameters can reproduce, and detectability is governed by the first surviving term. For example, unknown drift in testing-effort reproduces the linear term, leaving a quadratic survivor and raising the requirement to $N^{4/5}$; in general the critical scale is $N^{2q/(2q+1)}$ for a survivor of order $q$. We obtain the limiting-law of the estimator, the null likelihood ratio distribution, and confidence sets that may be unbounded.

papers.title: A Bayesian-Geometric Reading of Classical Model-Based Optimal Design
papers.authors: Mohamed Tarek
papers.abstract: The classical model-based optimal design criteria (D-, T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality) are usually motivated via the Cramér--Rao bound as optimizing scalar functions of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). This paper offers a complementary reading in which each criterion appears asymptotically as $N \to \infty$ as the leading-order term of an expected dissimilarity between prior and posterior, with the FIM entering through the Bernstein--von Mises limit. The Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence of the posterior relative to the prior recovers D-optimality (classically known); a reverse KL of the prior relative to the posterior recovers T-optimality (here defined as maximization of the trace of the FIM, following one common convention) and its weighted-trace generalization; and a first-order approximation of the squared 2-Wasserstein distance recovers L-, C- and A-optimality. The five criteria emerge as instances of a common Bayesian-geometric template, indexed by three choices: the dissimilarity, the prior parametrization, and the approximation scheme used to evaluate it (e.g.\ Taylor expansions of the matrix square root). For the weighted criteria, the Gaussian prior covariance encodes the criterion's weight matrix, so any choice of weights corresponds to a specific prior in the family. The T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality derivations appear novel to the best of my knowledge. A sixth criterion, E-optimality, is recovered not as an independent expected-dissimilarity limit but as a min-max robustification of C-optimality against uncertainty in the modeler's prior direction. The framework is extended to distinguish between a designer's prior over unknown parameters at design time and a modeler's prior used for posterior inference, recovering the classical expected information gain objective as a special case.

papers.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
papers.authors: Tao Li; Hai-Bing Fu; Lei-Hua Liu
papers.abstract: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet inflation. Starting from the quadratic perturbation actions, we construct the two-mode Hamiltonians and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing amplitudes and angles. Although the tensor speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss--Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We track the squeezing dynamics from the subhorizon to the superhorizon regime and evaluate the Nielsen wave-function complexity of the resulting two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation in the squeezing amplitudes, while the unwrapped squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Consequently, the circuit complexity is controlled mainly by the amplitude evolution. A positive coupling enhances the scalar complexity but slightly suppresses the tensor complexity for the benchmarks considered. These opposite trends show that scalar and tensor Gaussian states retain distinct information about the same modified inflationary background even when tensor propagation is luminal.

papers.title: GVT3D: Gesture-Vision-Text Token Enrichment for 3D Embodied Reference Understanding
papers.authors: Vimarsh Shah; Dulanga Weerakoon; Ajinkya Deshpande; Saksham Agarwal; Nilesh Bhatia et al.
papers.abstract: Natural human-robot interaction requires robots to interpret language and gestures within a 3D environment to support tasks such as pick-and-place and object retrieval. 3D Embodied Reference Understanding (3D-ERU) supports this by identifying the 3D location of a target object from a scene (point-cloud) containing a human pointing gesture and an accompanying language description. However, current 3D-ERU models lack alignment of cross-modal representations and incur high processing costs that increase with the point-cloud's size. To address this, we propose GVT3D, which employs an Embodied Fusion module that jointly models language, gesture, and vision inputs within a shared embedding space, promoting cross-modal alignment. We additionally introduce a foveation approach that selectively processes the point cloud within a coarse region around the estimated pointing direction to reduce computations. GVT3D achieves ~8% higher accuracy and foveation enables 2.95x faster execution while maintaining comparable accuracy, relative to prior 3D-ERU models.

papers.title: Weak uniqueness and autonomous approximation for the SLE-reversible Weil-Petersson response diffusion
papers.authors: Chunhao Cai
papers.abstract: We study the self-consistent common-noise equation associated with the Weil--Petersson response differential of the rotationally marked SLE welding probability. For $0<κ\leq4$, we prove joint weak uniqueness among continuous adapted weak solutions whose law at each deterministic time is the welding probability, and obtain the Markov property in the original filtration. A conditional Gaussian lift and capacity localization give the required $L^1$ generator-range density. Identification with the canonical law gives stationarity and reversibility. We also construct autonomous Fejér and Poisson regularizations with pathwise-unique global strong solutions. Their joint state-noise laws converge to the canonical law for every initial probability absolutely continuous with respect to the welding probability.

papers.title: SphereFlow: Missing Modality Imputation via Geometric Transport on Hypersphere
papers.authors: Huihan Wang; Juncheng Wang; Yuxiang Feng; Wenlong Hou; Guoqi Yu et al.
papers.abstract: Missing modality imputation aims to synthesize unobserved modalities from observed ones. Existing methods treat each modality as living on its own latent manifold, forcing the generator to learn a long, unstructured jump between them. We present SphereFlow, which takes a fundamentally different view: by projecting all modalities into a shared hyperspherical latent space via a frozen self-supervised encoder, cross-modal imputation reduces to short-range geometric transport between nearby points on the sphere. Realizing this idea with flow matching, however, exposes two geometric conflicts: the standard Gaussian noise source is catastrophically mismatched with the unit-norm data manifold, and the linear interpolation path departs the sphere surface into a region where the decoder has no training signal. We resolve both with simple, geometry-aware modifications: replacing the noise source with the observed-modality latent so that the velocity field learns only the cross-modal displacement, and training the decoder with a time-weighted loss that extends its domain to the near-surface region traversed by the flow. We prove that this data-as-source formulation reduces the worst-case off-manifold deviation from a quantity that grows with the latent dimension to a small, dimension-independent bound governed by inter-modality similarity. Experiments on BraTS multi-modal MRI imputation and CT-MRI translation demonstrate state-of-the-art generation fidelity across all settings, while downstream brain tumor segmentation with our imputed data closes roughly eighty percent of the gap to the full-modality oracle. Code is available at https://github.com/WTHH031230/SphereFlow.

papers.title: CaliSplat: Sparse Gaussian Fitting and Calibrated Rate Allocation for Image Compression
papers.authors: Zhenbang Zhang; Zhengquan Luo; Kai Zhao; Zhiqiang Xu
papers.abstract: 2D Gaussian representations provide an explicit and lightweight alternative for image representation, enabling fast deterministic decoding without a heavy neural synthesis network. However, existing per-image Gaussian codecs still require costly image-specific optimization to determine how limited Gaussian capacity should be distributed across heterogeneous regions. We introduce CaliSplat, an optimization-efficient Gaussian image codec that selectively explores candidate representations and globally allocates a constrained Gaussian budget. We exploit the closed-form reconstruction error of the single-Gaussian case as an inexpensive measure of local difficulty, fitting higher-capacity candidates only in regions where additional Gaussians are likely to be useful. To reduce selection errors caused by mismatched convergence rates across candidate sizes, a small set of longer-horizon fits is used to calibrate short-horizon distortion estimates before global budget-aware selection. The selected representation is then compressed into a bitstream. Across standard and large image datasets, CaliSplat achieves competitive or superior rate--distortion performance while reducing per-image fitting time by $3.0\times$--$15.7\times$ compared with representative Gaussian codecs. It further maintains high-throughput deterministic decoding at $175.9$--$478.2$~MP/s. These results demonstrate that content-adaptive Gaussian compression can substantially reduce per-image optimization cost while preserving strong reconstruction quality and efficient explicit decoding.

papers.title: Aero-VPA: Few-Step Flow-Matching Control over Non-Reconstructive JEPA Latents for Agile Flight on Edge Hardware
papers.authors: Yeonseok Lee
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generalize across tasks, but their autoregressive decoders need sequential forward passes in proportion to the action horizon, each bounded below on embedded aerial platforms by streaming billions of parameters from memory. We present Aero-VPA, a lightweight Vision-Predictor-Action architecture for 3D navigation on edge hardware. A compact RGB-D Vision Transformer and a five-head ensemble predictor, trained without pixel reconstruction, forecast the next latent state; a Conditional Flow Matching solver generates a velocity and yaw-rate chunk in two Euler steps, so each decision takes five sequential network evaluations; and the ensemble dispersion drives an uncertainty fallback. Version 1 specified the architecture, deployment and protocol without results. This version reports the first closed-loop evaluation: PX4 software-in-the-loop simulation of quadrotor missions in procedurally generated forests. Behaviour cloning failed on all 60 missions despite open-loop errors of 0.02-0.04 m/s: the policy copies its last command, a copycat form of causal confusion. DAgger with a privileged, safety-gated supervisor gave the first successes but plateaued at 11.1-21.1% across six checkpoints. A map-free runtime shield with a 15 s depth memory, barrier constraints, a cap on motion outside the 73-degree field of view and backoff along the flown path raised the first DAgger policy's success on 180 paired missions from 21.1% to 52.2% (95% CI [45.0, 59.4]; exact McNemar p = 1.2 x 10^-10) and cut its crashes from 72.2% to 22.2%, while timeouts rose from 2.8% to 23.3%. All six checkpoints gained 30.0-34.4 percentage points, at mean speeds of 1.16-1.36 m/s. The code (https://github.com/ylee-sling/Aero-VPA), the trained policy (72.6 MB, https://huggingface.co/ylee-sling/aero-vpa) and the full benchmark dataset are public.

papers.title: IGSW: Multi-Weather Urban Scene Reconstruction with Intrinsic-Decoupled Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Zhongquan Wang; Long Cao; Peijia Xie; Senlei Ma; Jie Li et al.
papers.abstract: High-fidelity weather editing of 4D scenes can support end-to-end training and closed-loop simulation for autonomous driving. Combining generative image editing with dynamic Gaussian representations enables multi-weather scene reconstruction, but weather-edited images often contain structural distortions. Directly fitting their appearance may propagate errors from teacher images into the reconstructed 4D scene, compromising the original scene structure and temporal continuity. To address these challenges, we propose IGSW, a two-stage framework that combines intrinsic-decoupled 4D Gaussian scene modeling with structure-preserving weather refinement. In Stage I, background Gaussian appearance is decomposed into weather-shared albedo and normals and weather-specific irradiance and residuals. Weather teacher images generated by a diffusion-based image editing model and intrinsic maps estimated by a diffusion-based inverse renderer provide feature-level soft supervision for stable structure and illumination changes. In Stage II, a structure-preservation gate combines semantic conflicts with cross-weather intrinsic discrepancies to suppress unreliable teacher regions. Per-Gaussian weather transport variables and target-weather branches then strengthen the desired weather appearance over the intrinsic-decoupled scene. Experiments on nuScenes and Waymo show that IGSW achieves the highest content similarity and semantic consistency and the lowest temporal error among the compared methods, while retaining pronounced weather-dependent illumination and atmosphere. The project page is available at https://akaxi6.github.io/IGSW/ .

papers.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
papers.authors: Guowei Yan; Dan Zhuang; Long Feng
papers.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. We combine calibrated p-values from a matched pair of fixed- and proportional-order statistics using the Cauchy combination rule to adapt to unknown sparsity. For localization, the estimated change point is selected from the component scan with the smallest p-value. Simulation studies demonstrate generally satisfactory size calibration, competitive detection power, and effective localization across different sparsity levels. An application to semiconductor manufacturing data further illustrates the practical utility of the proposed methods.

papers.title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
papers.authors: Hesam Hosseini; Jinpei Zhao; Masahito Hayashi
papers.abstract: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.

papers.title: EndoS3:Endoscopic Semantic Splatting SLAM
papers.authors: Mona Sheikh Zeinoddin; Benjamin Wright; Zafer Tandogdu; Greg Shaw; Evangelos Mazomenos et al.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Despite advances in 3D surgical scene understanding, semantic simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM) remains under-explored for two key reasons. First, it requires solving three challenging tasks in parallel: camera pose tracking, high-fidelity deformable reconstruction, and semantic mapping, making progress particularly demanding. Second, the scarcity of datasets providing the necessary ground truth to evaluate all three tasks comprehensively under conditions that closely reflect real surgical procedures environments. Method: We propose EndoS3, a Gaussian Splatting-based semantic SLAM framework that uses instance masks to guide all three tasks. An instance-level motion decomposition module separates static and dynamic instances by evaluating residual flow after compensating for camera motion, accounting for flow noise and comparing motion across neighbouring instances. The camera is tracked against the static Gaussians, while an instance-aware warp field gives each dynamic instance its own control nodes and deformation network. A semantic node allocation module redistributes a fixed node budget across instances according to their size and non-rigidity. We also introduce CRCD++, an ex-vivo Cholecystectomy dataset with RGB-D frames, camera pose and instance annotations for full semantic SLAM evaluation. Results: EndoS3 surpasses all state-of-the-art general-purpose and surgical semantic SLAM methods in tracking, reconstruction and semantic mapping on the CRCD++ and SemSup datasets. Conclusion: Semantic-aware motion and deformation modelling is vital to surgical semantic SLAM. EndoS3 and CRCD++ offer a method and benchmark for improved geometric and semantic understanding in endoscopy.

papers.title: CLOCs-R: Radar-Assisted Camera-LiDAR Fusion for Long-Range Object Detection
papers.authors: Richard Beuck; John Nguyen; Sudip Dhakal
papers.abstract: Long-range 3D object detection remains difficult for autonomous vehicles because LiDAR returns become sparse and camera evidence weakens with distance, while automotive radar keeps returning measurements far beyond both. We present CLOCs-R, an extension of the CLOCs candidate-level fusion framework that adds radar evidence to camera-LiDAR rescoring. Radar returns are accumulated over several sweeps, compensated for ego-motion, and associated with each pre-NMS 3D candidate through a range-dependent gate. Compact features summarizing support, Doppler speed and spread, range residual, and offset are then appended to every camera-LiDAR pair before a lightweight fusion network rescores the candidates. We first verify that our fusion implementation reproduces CLOCs on KITTI. We then evaluate on the daytime clear-weather subset of the aiMotive dataset, reporting distance-binned metrics out to 200 m with frozen SECOND and Cascade R-CNN detectors. Camera-LiDAR CLOCs improves on SECOND up to 50 m but degrades beyond it. A residual scoring variant, introduced post hoc, corrects SECOND's score instead of replacing it and recovers most of this loss. Radar consistently improves BEV AP at 30-50 m (0.857 to 0.870), but beyond 50 m its gain is small (+0.003 center-distance AP), within seed variation, and CLOCs-R with residual scoring is statistically tied with LiDAR-only SECOND. Our analysis attributes the limited long-range benefit to weak separation of true and false detections by radar features, scarce far-range training positives, poor camera evidence at distance, and missing LiDAR proposals that rescoring cannot recover. We report all as-designed and post hoc results side by side.

papers.title: State Evolution and Universality of Iterated Linear Programs for the Binary Perceptron
papers.authors: Jianan Zhang; Shuangping Li
papers.abstract: The binary perceptron is a random constraint satisfaction problem that asks for a sign vector satisfying a system of random linear inequalities. Its solution space has a strikingly extreme geometry: at every positive constraint density, all but a vanishing fraction of the solutions are isolated. Yet polynomial-time algorithms find solutions at small enough constraint density, which raises the question of how efficient algorithms navigate such a landscape. Linear programming is a natural algorithm to study here, but its analysis has so far been limited to a single round. Li, Schramm, and Zhou (STOC 2025) analyzed one linear program followed by iterative rounding.   In this work, we overcome this limitation and give a precise analysis of iterated linear programming for the binary perceptron. (1) For Gaussian matrices and any fixed number of rounds, we characterize the iterated linear programs exactly through a deterministic state-evolution recursion. (2) Adding a final rounding step, we obtain a randomized polynomial-time algorithm for the binary perceptron. Numerical evaluations of the recursion provide evidence that it succeeds at constraint density $α=0.60$ with zero margin, well beyond the range $α\le0.1$ guaranteed by the single-LP analysis and $α\approx0.327$ (Jo and Lee, 2026), the best guarantee so far. (3) We establish universality, showing that the same characterization holds for matrices with i.i.d. entries drawn from any centered, unit-variance subgaussian law.   The key idea of our proof is that, although conditioning on earlier rounds makes the matrix non-Gaussian, its conditional law can be computed explicitly and remains close to a Gaussian law, so the convex Gaussian min-max theorem applies in every round. For universality, we compare Gaussian and subgaussian matrices through the Lindeberg principle, using a regularized version of each linear program.

papers.title: Bezier-GP: Bezier-Surface-Based Gaussian Process for Chips-on-Wafer Warpage Modeling
papers.authors: Sangyup Lee; Xiao Liu; Jianjun Shi
papers.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. The proposed framework combines wafer-level point-cloud metrology data with wafer-map layout information to construct chip-region-level Bezier surface patches, imposes continuity constraints between neighboring patches, and represents the resulting chips-on-wafer surface through a compact free-control-point vector. A GP is then introduced in this low-dimensional representation to model wafer-to-wafer variation, chip-region-level spatial dependence, and provide uncertainty quantification. Numerical experiments, using an ASC wafer-map layout, demonstrate that the proposed framework can reconstruct chips-on-wafer surfaces, preserve chip-region-level geometric interpretability, and recover population-level mean and covariance structures under a controlled multi-wafer simulation setting. The results suggest that Bezier-GP provides a measurement-driven statistical modeling foundation for connecting wafer-level metrology data to chip-region-level warpage analysis in semiconductor manufacturing.

papers.title: Attack-Aware Intrusion Risk Monitoring for Aerial Surveillance via Probabilistic Signal Temporal Logic
papers.authors: Xinhao Yan; Kenji Kashima; Bo Chen; Hailong Huang
papers.abstract: This paper considers online intrusion-risk assessment and graded warning for unmanned aerial vehicles under bounded measurement attacks. To address this problem, we develop a monitoring framework that combines trusted state estimation, attack-aware risk assessment, and probabilistic signal temporal logic (PrSTL). Trusted observations support recursive state estimation, while potentially attacked observations inform integrity testing and intrusion-risk assessment. The key contribution is a confidence-set construction that combines normalized innovation statistics with physical attack bounds to characterize admissible measurement biases. The resulting family of bias-corrected Gaussian posteriors yields an upper bound on the probability of occupying a no-fly zone or its surrounding safety margin. Confidence guarantees and finite-cover numerical certificates quantify the reliability of this risk envelope, which is evaluated with or without an integrity alarm. The PrSTL monitor analyzes the resulting risk sequence to distinguish ordered, persistent, and repeated risk and produces graded warnings with explicit robustness margins and supporting windows. We validate the monitor in flight experiments with a Crazyflie quadrotor tracked by a Vicon motion capture system. Controlled comparisons quantify the contributions of individual monitoring components. Prescribed risk profiles verify the temporal semantics and illustrate how distinct risk patterns produce different warning levels.

papers.title: Differentiable topology optimization for high-fidelity acoustic holography beyond the thin-element approximation
papers.authors: Pradosh Pritam Dash; Costas D. Arvanitis
papers.abstract: Acoustic holography in the megahertz range can impact applications from manufacturing and non-destructive testing to transcranial ultrasound. Designing lens topologies for complex holograms in the sub-megahertz to low-megahertz regime most relevant to transcranial therapy is difficult because wave propagation through an acoustically thick lens cannot be ignored. Here we show that the heterogeneous angular spectrum approach (HASA), which admits in-plane varying speed-of-sound maps and supports rapid differentiable optimization with the Adam optimizer, can generate three-dimensional lens topologies directly. With it we quantify the failure of the thin-element approximation (TEA) at these frequencies, where lenses enter an acoustically thick regime (thickness L much greater than the wavelength) governed by refractive walk-off, and we introduce a dimensionless refractive walk-off number Nw that defines a frequency-dependent operating regime. Topology optimization outperformed TEA-based design in all 45 configurations tested, with the largest structural gains at or below 1 MHz; for high-numerical-aperture designs the fidelity at 1 MHz matched that at 2 MHz, while structural similarity was highest at 0.5 MHz. The sub-megahertz to low-megahertz window is therefore a favorable operating regime for high-fidelity transcranial holography rather than one to be avoided. Free-field hydrophone measurements of 3D-printed lenses reproduced the designed patterns, and because the framework also accounts for aberration in heterogeneous media, patient-specific lenses corrected skull-induced aberration in simulation and ex vivo experiment, generalized across skull segments, and shaped volumetric beams through the human skull. Together these results provide a framework for designing simple, economical, and high-performance ultrasound systems.

papers.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
papers.authors: Kailing Li; Ruoxuan Zhang; Zheyuan Zhou; Boyang Chu; Yingshan Lei et al.
papers.abstract: Video games provide a practical setting for collecting vision-language-action (VLA) data, whose acquisition in physical environments is costly. Existing datasets, however, remain limited by restricted game coverage, sparse language supervision, or temporal hierarchies that do not necessarily reflect changes in task objectives. We introduce AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions. AceAction organizes demonstrations around complete tasks, linking overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions to temporally aligned visual observations and keyboard-and-mouse actions. To construct these annotations, we develop a vision-language model pipeline that identifies subgoals from changes in objectives or interaction targets, anchors navigation goals to visually recognizable waypoints, and composes adjacent subgoals into task instructions. The resulting demonstrations cover navigation, reconnaissance, combat, interaction, and recovery, with explicit stage boundaries that connect task progression to fine-grained control. We assess annotation quality through model-based verification and human inspection. An audit of 500 trajectories yields a 95.8% pass rate across independent reviewer assessments. AceAction provides a data foundation for studying how agents execute, combine, and switch skills to follow complex instructions in dynamic game environments.

papers.title: Fermi-LAT Detection of Extended GeV Emission toward the Middle-aged Supernova Remnant G156.2+05.7
papers.authors: Wei-Liang Xu; Qing-Wen Tang; Long Li
papers.abstract: We analyse 17 years of Fermi-LAT $γ$-ray data toward the middle-aged supernova remnant (SNR) G156.2+05.7, supplemented by radio and CO observations and by published X-ray constraints. An extended $γ$-ray source is detected, well described by a 2D Gaussian template ($R_{68} \sim 0.84^\circ$). This description is preferred over a foreground CO template, whereas the Gaussian and a uniform disc are statistically indistinguishable under the AIC. The spectrum shows evidence for curvature, with a log-parabola preferred over a power law at the $\approx 3.4σ$ level. Multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution (SED) modelling, under the adopted assumptions, suggests a leptonic--hadronic joint scenario consistent with the data, with the Fermi-LAT spectrum favouring a hadronic contribution over a purely leptonic interpretation. However, the proton-dominated alternative remains competitive, so the partition of the GeV emission is model-dependent. In the adopted leptonic--hadronic model, the electron population accounts for the radio synchrotron emission and a leptonic $γ$-ray component, while a steep proton population contributes the remaining hadronic $γ$-rays. Adopting a reference distance $d = 2.7$ kpc, the fitted electron cutoff ($E_{e,\mathrm{cut}}\approx 1.2$ TeV) is compatible with the thermal-dominated X-ray emission, while the proton cutoff is fixed by assumption at $1$ TeV. The northeast and southwest quadrants show enhanced $γ$-ray emission, which may be related to a clumpy or asymmetric surrounding medium. A correspondence with the directions of optical H$α$ filaments is suggested by the quadrant orientation but is not yet established. No significant long-term flux variability is found, consistent with steady emission from an extended source.

papers.title: Mamba3R: Fixed-Capacity Selective State Memory for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction
papers.authors: Zhenxiang Xiong; Tianchen Deng; Nailin Wang; Lei Zhao; Guole Shen et al.
papers.abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction must maintain geometric quality over long inputs within a fixed GPU budget. A pretrained recurrent model provides bounded state, but freezing its backbone also fixes its learned state-observation interactions. We introduce Mamba3R, a jointly designed state-memory adapter that provides a trainable adaptation path without updating the backbone or task heads. A selective state-space mixer jointly transforms native state features and a fixed-capacity auxiliary memory, explicit read and write paths carry information across frames, and a decomposed feedback path regulates what the added memory feeds back. Only 1.28 million adapter parameters are trained. Under a shared periodic-reset protocol, it lowers trajectory error and improves accumulated surface and depth accuracy over recurrent baselines on public indoor and outdoor datasets and robot-recorded traversals, gaining up to 40 percent on one metric. Matched comparisons support both the choice of the mixing operator and the utility of carrying the auxiliary memory across frames. Allocated memory remains unchanged and throughput moves by at most 1.4 percent from one to two thousand frames. Replaying its recorded traversals offline, the platform's RTX 4060 averages 11.7 frames per second within 5.1 GiB with the same checkpoint, a mean throughput covering the 10 Hz sensor rate.

papers.title: Two-Layer Random ReLU Networks Can Separate Disjoint Classes
papers.authors: Yichen Liu; Jianbin Yang
papers.abstract: Set separation by continuous linear functionals is fundamental in functional analysis and convex optimization and underlies binary classification in machine learning. Support vector machines provide maximum-margin affine separators for linearly separable data, while kernel methods represent nonlinear decision rules through linear separation in a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space. We study when two classes, not necessarily convex or linearly separable in the input space, can be separated with positive margin by finite ReLU networks and by random ReLU features.   At the deterministic level, we prove that positive-margin separation by a finite ReLU network is equivalent to the existence of finite closed convex covers whose opposite-label members have positive pairwise distances, and exactly two hidden layers suffice. For random separation, suppose each class is represented as a finite union of nonempty closed convex cells, possibly unbounded. If every opposite-label cell pair has positive distance and its closed difference cone is pointed, then two independent random ReLU layers yield a common positive-margin affine separator with high probability.   The first layer separates the feature image of each negative cell from the feature image of the positive class by a hyperplane through the origin. It also controls all cross-class distances uniformly. The second layer combines cellwise scores through Chebyshev polynomials and realizes the resulting polynomial using Gaussian Hermite features, followed by a uniform finite-width approximation. With the remaining geometric, bias, and confidence parameters fixed, each sufficient width is quadratic in the largest Gaussian width of a spherical difference-cone section, hence at most linear in its span dimension. An example shows that this squared Gaussian-width dependence is sharp for both layers.

papers.title: Accurate representation of the continuum orbital in a Gaussian basis set: application to Auger decay rates
papers.authors: Dibyendu Mahato; Saikat Roy; Wojciech Skomorowski
papers.abstract: Many processes in chemistry and physics, such as autoionization, photoionization, or electron-impact collisions, involve unbound electrons. Despite their importance, theoretical methods for modeling continuum electrons remain significantly less developed than those for purely bound electronic states. Here we present a novel approach for treating continuum electrons within Gaussian-based quantum chemistry. The method represents continuum orbital in a discrete basis of standard Gaussian-type orbitals (GTOs), where the continuum wave function is obtained by solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation with proper boundary conditions using an analytical representation of the Green's function in an auxiliary GTO basis set. The resulting continuum orbital is multicentered and multichannel, providing a rigorous description of scattering states. As an initial application of the new methodology, we compute Auger decay rates for several atomic and molecular systems, including Ne, H$_2$O, CO$_2$, and Ar. We demonstrate a consistent improvement of the results with increasing the quality of the continuum representation. We show also that higher-order electron-correlation effects in the bound domain are essential for an accurate treatment of satellite transitions. The present formalism therefore provides a systematically improvable Gaussian-based framework for continuum-electron problems that is fully compatible with standard quantum chemistry methods.

papers.title: The Characteristic Initial Value Problem for the 3D Compressible Euler Equations
papers.authors: Jared Speck; Sifan Yu
papers.abstract: We prove local existence and uniqueness, propagation of Sobolev regularity, and continuation criteria results for the characteristic initial value problem for the 3D compressible Euler equations. This is the Cauchy problem with initial data given on a pair of transversally intersecting (acoustically) null hypersurfaces. The region of existence in our main theorem is a future-neighborhood of the union of the data null hypersurfaces, where the size of the neighborhood depends on various norms of the data as well as the structure of the data null hypersurfaces. We allow for any equation of state with positive sound speed, and we do not make any symmetry, irrotationality, or isentropicity assumptions. Our analysis relies on the geometric formulation of the flow derived in [Speck19], which decomposes the equations into a "wave-part" coupled to a "transport-div-curl" part. Compared to Rendall's celebrated solution of the characteristic initial value problem for wave equations [Rendall90], substantial new ideas are needed to handle the fact that the compressible Euler equations are more complicated than pure wave equations.

papers.title: SettleSplat: Monocular Gaussian Mapping under In-View Scene Changes
papers.authors: Anh Thuan Tran; Xiyun Song; Yubin Zhou; Heather Yu; Jana Kosecka et al.
papers.abstract: Online 3D Gaussian mapping enables fast and high-fidelity novel view synthesis, with broad applications in augmented reality, robotics, and autonomous systems. However, many current methods assume static scenes or filter out dynamics as outliers. In this paper, we study in-view scene changes where objects are manipulated in front of the camera within a single online sequence, unlike prior works that detect changes outside the camera view or between separate captures. This setting entangles transient and persistent dynamics, as objects can be distractors while moving and persistent once they settle. While recent studies start to address distractors by removing them for clean static background, in-view scene changes remain underexplored. To resolve this, we present SettleSplat, a monocular mapping system that maintains up-to-date 3D Gaussian maps under such changes. Specifically, we lift coarse per-pixel uncertainty into Gaussian dynamicity field, then prune transient ones. For persistent changes, we derive geometric contradictions weighted by parameter-free rendered depth uncertainty to separate true changes from under-optimized regions.
